cond_0001.intro: The Labelling Strategy Associate Director provides regulatory labelling expertise, typically for more complex drug projects, to the Global Regulatory Submission Team (GRST)/Global Regulatory Execution Team (GRET), and cross functional Product Labelling Teams (PLT). This individual leads the development/implementation of the labelling strategy and maintenance of Core Product Information and [Location masked]/European Union ([Location masked]) Market Product Information (MPI) for assigned marketed or pipeline products.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Ensures that the labelling process is followed through the lifecycle of the product.
Ensure all work is performed in accordance with established procedures, regulatory requirements and GxPs.
Leads the development of the labelling strategy, in line with the overall regulatory strategy for the product, by interpretation of regulations, guidance and competitor analyses, anticipating and communicating the wider impacts of the strategy and the long-term consequences for the product and the wider portfolio.
Leads the PLT in the preparation and maintenance of high-quality Core Prescribing Information, [Location masked] Quality review of Documents (QRD), [Location masked] Prescribing Information (PI), Instructions For Use (IFUs) through to Senior Leader approval with the aim of achieving advantageous labelling.
Leads the development of labelling negotiation strategies, anticipating HA perspectives.
Provides labelling expertise for assigned products regarding language, placement and regulatory content detail for CPI and MPI in line with company procedures, regional labelling regulations and guidance.
Provides clarity regarding applicable labelling requirements and expectations in complex situations to relevant stakeholders, including risk insight and proposing mitigations.
Evaluates, interprets and communicates global regulations and trends on labelling and any business impact these might have on product labelling.
Ensures appropriate communication across Labelling subfunctions.
Able to justify and communicate the labelling rationale to Senior Leaders to enable effective decision making.
Leads the development of target labelling documents as appropriate.

University Degree in Science or related discipline
3 To 5 years pharmaceutical experience, including regulatory experience, preferably working with labelling
Labelling expertise in Core Data Sheet and [Location masked] labelling

Excellent verbal and written communication skills

Ability to think strategically, appropriately assess risks and formulate strategies to manage risk

This individual leads the development/implementation of the labelling strategy and maintenance of Core Product Information and [Location masked]/European Union ([Location masked]) Market Product Information (MPI) for assigned marketed or pipeline products.

Ensures that the labelling process is followed through the lifecycle of the product.
Ensure all work is performed in accordance with established procedures, regulatory requirements and GxPs.
Leads the development of the labelling strategy, in line with the overall regulatory strategy for the product, by interpretation of regulations, guidance and competitor analyses, anticipating and communicating the wider impacts of the strategy and the long-term consequences for the product and the wider portfolio.

Evaluates, interprets and communicates global regulations and trends on labelling and any business impact these might have on product labelling.

cond_0083.responsibilities: Ensures that the labelling process is followed through the lifecycle of the product. • Ensure all work is performed in accordance with established procedures, regulatory requirements and GxPs. • Leads the development of the labelling strategy, in line with the overall regulatory strategy for the product, by interpretation of regulations, guidance and competitor analyses, anticipating and communicating the wider impacts of the strategy and the long-term consequences for the product and the wider portfolio. • Leads the PLT in the preparation and maintenance of high-quality Core Prescribing Information, [Location masked] Quality review of Documents (QRD), [Location masked] Prescribing Information (PI), Instructions For Use (IFUs) through to Senior Leader approval with the aim of achieving advantageous labelling. • Leads the development of labelling negotiation strategies, anticipating HA perspectives. • Provides labelling expertise for assigned products regarding language, placement and regulatory content detail for CPI and MPI in line with company procedures, regional labelling regulations and guidance. • Provides clarity regarding applicable labelling requirements and expectations in complex situations to relevant stakeholders, including risk insight and proposing mitigations • Evaluates, interprets and communicates global regulations and trends on labelling and any business impact these might have on product labelling • Ensures appropriate communication across Labelling subfunctions • Able to justify and communicate the labelling rationale to Senior Leaders to enable effective decision making. • Leads the development of target labelling documents as appropriate
cond_0083.requirements:
Demonstrated expertise in Core Data Sheet and [Location masked] labelling, with a proven track record of leading teams and labelling negotiations with Health Authorities (e.g. FDA, EMA).
Bachelor's degree in Science or a related discipline required; advanced degree strongly preferred.
Minimum 5 years of pharmaceutical experience, including substantial regulatory experience, with significant time working in labelling.
Advanced knowledge of labelling regulations and guidances.
Exceptional verbal and written communication skills.
Strong command of attention to detail and accuracy.
Extensive multi-cultural awareness and sensitivity; proven ability to communicate and negotiate effectively across diverse cultures.
Deep expertise in assimilating clinical and scientific information and presenting it concisely.
Proven ability to think strategically, rigorously assess risks, and formulate robust strategies to manage them.
Strong ability to build and maintain relationships across formal and informal networks.
Exceptional negotiation skills; an active listener with a demonstrated ability to build consensus.

Ability to assimilate clinical and scientific information and present it concisely

This individual leads the development and implementation of the labelling strategy and maintenance of Core Product Information and [Location masked]/European Union ([Location masked]) Market Product Information (MPI) for assigned marketed or pipeline products.

Ensures all work is performed in accordance with established procedures, regulatory requirements and GxPs.

Provides clarity regarding applicable labelling requirements and expectations in complex situations to relevant stakeholders, including risk insight and proposing mitigations.
Evaluates, interprets and communicates global regulations and trends on labelling and any business impact these might have on product labelling.

cond_0501.intro: The Labelling Strategy Associate Director provides regulatory labelling expertise, typically for more complex drug projects, to the Global Regulatory Submission Team (GRST)/Global Regulatory Execution Team (GRET), and cross functional Product Labelling Teams (PLT). A large part of this role involves staying in regular contact with these teams and actively contributing to labelling decisions. This individual leads the development and implementation of the labelling strategy and maintenance of Core Product Information and [Location masked]/European Union ([Location masked]) Market Product Information (MPI) for assigned marketed or pipeline products.
cond_0501.responsibilities:
Ensures that the labelling process is followed through the lifecycle of the product.
Ensure all work is performed in accordance with established procedures, regulatory requirements and GxPs.
Leads the development of the labelling strategy, in line with the overall regulatory strategy for the product, by interpretation of regulations, guidance and competitor analyses, actively communicating the wider impacts of the strategy and the long-term consequences for the product and the wider portfolio.
Leads the PLT in the preparation and maintenance of high-quality Core Prescribing Information, [Location masked] Quality review of Documents (QRD), [Location masked] Prescribing Information (PI), Instructions For Use (IFUs) through to Senior Leader approval with the aim of achieving advantageous labelling.
Leads the development of labelling negotiation strategies, anticipating HA perspectives.
Provides labelling expertise for assigned products regarding language, placement and regulatory content detail for CPI and MPI in line with company procedures, regional labelling regulations and guidance.
Provides clarity regarding applicable labelling requirements and expectations in complex situations to relevant stakeholders, including risk insight and proposing mitigations — regularly walking stakeholders through the reasoning and handling questions directly.
Evaluates, interprets and communicates global regulations and trends on labelling and any business impact these might have on product labelling.
Ensures ongoing communication across Labelling subfunctions.
Able to justify and communicate the labelling rationale to Senior Leaders to enable effective decision making.
Leads the development of target labelling documents as appropriate.

cond_0648.intro: The Labelling Strategy Associate Director provides regulatory labelling expertise, typically for more complex drug projects, working alongside the Global Regulatory Submission Team (GRST)/Global Regulatory Execution Team (GRET), and cross-functional Product Labelling Teams (PLT). In this role, you will coordinate the development and implementation of the labelling strategy and support the maintenance of Core Product Information and [Location masked]/European Union ([Location masked]) Market Product Information (MPI) for assigned marketed or pipeline products.
